query: Official GitHub Actions documentation matrix builds create releases upload release assets and artifact attestations site:docs.github.com
content:
**Primary Official Documentation (docs.github.com)**

The search query best matches GitHub's guide that combines all these topics in a modern, secure release pipeline:

### Core Page
**Using artifact attestations to establish provenance for builds**  
**URL**: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/using-artifact-attestations-to-establish-provenance-for-builds (or minor path variations such as `/security-guides/`)

This page demonstrates an end-to-end pattern using:
- `strategy.matrix` for multi-platform/architecture builds
- Creating a GitHub Release (`gh release create`)
- Uploading built binaries as release assets (`gh release upload`)
- Generating and attaching **artifact attestations** (cryptographically signed SLSA-style provenance using OIDC and GitHub's signing infrastructure)

It is the most relevant single resource as of 2026.

### Supporting Official Pages

**Matrix builds / strategy**
- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-what-your-workflow-does/running-variations-of-jobs-in-a-workflow
- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-jobs/using-a-matrix-for-your-jobs
- Key syntax: `strategy: matrix:` with arrays/objects, `include`/`exclude`, `matrix.*` context, `fail-fast`, and `max-parallel`.

**Creating releases and uploading release assets**
- https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/managing-releases-in-a-repository (includes automation guidance)
- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/using-github-cli-in-workflows (covers `gh release create` and `gh release upload`)
- Recommended pattern (official): Use the preinstalled `gh` CLI with `GITHUB_TOKEN` (requires `contents: write` permission). The older `actions/upload-release-asset` action is largely superseded.
- Related: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/automating-releases-with-continuous-integration

**Artifact attestations (provenance / SLSA)**
- Main guide (above)
- Overview: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/about-artifact-attestations (or similar path)
- Requires `id-token: write` and `attestations: write` permissions. Typically uses `actions/attest-build`, `gh attestation`, or equivalent official tooling to sign artifacts and link them back to the exact workflow run.

### Typical Combined Workflow Pattern (from official docs)

A standard secure release workflow follows this structure:

```yaml
name: Build, Release, and Attest

on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']

permissions:
  contents: write
  id-token: write
  attestations: write

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest]
        # Can extend to architecture, Go version, etc.
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build binary
        run: ./build.sh
      - name: Generate attestation for this build
        uses: actions/attest-build@v1  # or equivalent per current docs
        with:
          subject-path: './dist/myapp-*'
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: ./dist/*

release:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: build-*
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Create Release and upload assets + attestations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh release create ${{ github.ref_name }} \
            --title "Release ${{ github.ref_name }}" \
            --generate-notes
          gh release upload ${{ github.ref_name }} ./dist/*
```

**Key points from the docs**:
- Matrix jobs run in parallel for different platforms.
- Attestations provide verifiable provenance (who built it, in which workflow, from which commit).
- The release job uses `needs:` to wait for all matrix variants.
- Attestations can be viewed in the GitHub UI and consumed by dependency review or external verifiers (e.g., `sigstore` tools).

**Sources**: All links above are from `docs.github.com`. The artifact attestations guide is the authoritative reference that ties matrix builds, release creation, asset upload, and provenance together. Check the pages directly for the latest action versions and exact syntax, as GitHub updates these frequently.

## GitHub Actions

          
   Uploading artifacts to the linked artifacts page
   Verifying artifact attestations with the GitHub CLI
   Next steps

## Prerequisites

Before you start generating artifact attestations, you need to understand what they are and when you should use them. See Artifact attestations.

## Generating artifact attestations for your builds [...] ## Uploading artifacts to the linked artifacts page

We recommend uploading attested assets to your organization's linked artifacts page. This page displays artifacts' build history, deployment records, and storage details. You can use this data to prioritize security alerts or quickly connect vulnerable artifacts to their owning team, source code, and build run. For more information, see About linked artifacts.

The attest action automatically creates storage records on the linked artifacts page if both:

   The `push-to-registry` option is set to `true`
   The workflow that includes the action has the `artifact-metadata: write` permission

For an example workflow, see Uploading storage and deployment data to the linked artifacts page. [...] ## Generating artifact attestations for your builds

You can use GitHub Actions to generate artifact attestations that establish build provenance for artifacts such as binaries and container images.

To generate an artifact attestation, you must:

   Ensure you have the appropriate permissions configured in your workflow.
   Include a step in your workflow that uses the `attest` action.

When you run your updated workflows, they will build your artifacts and generate an artifact attestation that establishes build provenance. You can view attestations in your repository's Actions tab. For more information, see the `attest` repository.

### Generating build provenance for binaries

1.   In the workflow that builds the binary you would like to attest, add the following permissions.
